# nhl-api-ts

> TypeScript SDK and CLI for the public NHL web API (api-web.nhle.com) and stats API (api.nhle.com/stats/rest): teams, rosters, schedules, scores, boxscores, play-by-play, standings, player/team/skater/goalie stats, and NHL EDGE tracking. Node.js >= 24, ESM only, zero dependencies, no API key.

Key facts:

- `import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts'; const client = new NHLClient();` then `await client.<module>.<method>({ ...options })`.
- Modules: teams, standings, schedule, gameCenter, stats, edge, players, misc, helpers. Every method is async and takes one options object with camelCase keys.
- Every SDK method is also a CLI command: `npx nhl-api-ts <module-kebab> <method-kebab> [args] --compact` prints JSON.
- Seasons are `YYYYYYYY` (20232024). Game ids are `YYYYTTNNNN` (2023020280). Game type: 1 preseason, 2 regular, 3 playoffs.
- Stats API pages are capped at 100 rows. HTTP errors extend `NHLApiException`. Invalid input throws `RangeError`.

This file concatenates the documents listed in llms.txt. Generated by `pnpm docs:llms`. Do not edit.

<!-- README: README.md -->

# nhl-api-ts

TypeScript SDK **and** command line tool for the NHL API and NHL EDGE stats.

Every SDK method is also available as a CLI command.

- Zero runtime dependencies (uses the built-in `fetch`)
- Node.js >= 24, ESM only
- Fully typed

## Documentation

- [Concepts](docs/concepts.md): ID formats, the two NHL APIs, "now" redirects, pagination, retries
- [Errors](docs/errors.md): every error, its cause and the fix
- [Recipes](docs/recipes/): [filtered stats](docs/recipes/filter-skater-stats.md),
  [pagination](docs/recipes/paginate-stats.md), [live scores](docs/recipes/live-scores.md),
  [season-wide data](docs/recipes/season-wide-data.md), [retries](docs/recipes/retries.md),
  [CLI + jq](docs/recipes/cli-and-jq.md), [testing](docs/recipes/testing.md)
- [Examples](examples/): runnable scripts
- [API report](api-report.md): the full public TypeScript API
- [OpenAPI](openapi.yaml): every HTTP path the SDK calls
- [Migration guide](MIGRATION.md): from nhl-api-py
- For LLMs and agents: [llms.txt](llms.txt), [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt),
  [Agent Skill](skills/nhl-api-ts/SKILL.md)

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add nhl-api-ts      # SDK
pnpm add -g nhl-api-ts   # CLI (`nhl-api-ts` on your PATH)
# or run the CLI without installing:
npx nhl-api-ts --help
```

## SDK quick start

```ts
import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient();

const teams = await client.teams.teams();
const standings = await client.standings.leagueStandings();
const games = await client.schedule.dailySchedule();
```

Every method is `async` and takes a single options object:

```ts
await client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId: '2023020280' });
await client.edge.skaterDetail({ playerId: 8478402, season: 20232024 });
await client.stats.teamSummary({ startSeason: 20202021, endSeason: 20232024 });
```

IDs and seasons accept either strings or numbers.

## Configuration

```ts
const client = new NHLClient({
  debug: true,           // log each request URL to stderr (default false)
  timeout: 30,           // seconds (default 10)
  followRedirects: true, // "/now" endpoints redirect to today's data (default true)
});
```

## API modules

All methods below live on `client.<module>`. Parameters in `[brackets]` are
optional.

### teams

- `teams({ [date] })` — all teams with conference, division and `franchise_id`
- `teamRoster({ teamAbbr, season })`
- `franchises()`

### standings

- `leagueStandings({ [date], [season] })` — `season` uses that season's final standings
- `seasonStandingManifest()`

### schedule

- `dailySchedule({ [date] })` — date is validated/normalized (`2024-10-9` → `2024-10-09`)
- `weeklySchedule({ [date] })`
- `teamMonthlySchedule({ teamAbbr, [month] })`
- `teamWeeklySchedule({ teamAbbr, [date] })`
- `teamSeasonSchedule({ teamAbbr, season })`
- `calendarSchedule({ date })`
- `playoffCarousel({ season })`
- `playoffSeriesSchedule({ season, series })`
- `playoffBracket({ year })`

### gameCenter

- `boxscore({ gameId })`
- `playByPlay({ gameId })`
- `matchUp({ gameId })`
- `dailyScores({ [date] })`
- `shiftChartData({ gameId, [excludes] })`
- `seasonSeriesMatchup({ gameId })`
- `gameStory({ gameId })`

### stats

- `gametypesPerSeasonDirectoryByTeam({ teamAbbr })`
- `playerCareerStats({ playerId })`
- `playerGameLog({ playerId, seasonId, gameType })`
- `teamSummary({ startSeason, endSeason, [gameTypeId], [isGame], [isAggregate], [sortExpr], [start], [limit], [factCayenneExp], [defaultCayenneExp] })`
- `skaterStatsSummary({ startSeason, endSeason, [franchiseId], [gameTypeId], [aggregate], [sortExpr], [start], [limit], [factCayenneExp], [defaultCayenneExp] })`
- `skaterStatsWithQueryContext({ queryContext, reportType, [sortExpr], [aggregate], [start], [limit] })`
- `goalieStatsSummary({ startSeason, [endSeason], [statsType], [gameTypeId], [franchiseId], [aggregate], [sortExpr], [start], [limit], [factCayenneExp], [defaultCayenneExp] })`

### edge

Every EDGE method takes `[season]` and `[gameType]` (2 = regular season, the
default; 3 = playoffs). Without `season` the current season (`/now`) is used.

- Skaters (`{ playerId }`): `skaterDetail`, `skaterShotSpeedDetail`,
  `skaterSkatingSpeedDetail`, `skaterShotLocationDetail`,
  `skaterSkatingDistanceDetail`, `skaterComparison`, `skaterZoneTime`,
  `catSkaterDetail`
- Goalies (`{ playerId }`): `goalieDetail`, `goalieShotLocationDetail`,
  `goalie5v5Detail`, `goalieComparison`, `goalieSavePercentageDetail`,
  `catGoalieDetail`
- Teams (`{ teamId }`): `teamDetail`, `teamSkatingDistanceDetail`,
  `teamZoneTimeDetails`, `teamShotLocationDetail`, `teamShotSpeedDetail`,
  `teamSkatingSpeedDetail`
- Landing pages (no id): `skaterLanding`, `goalieLanding`, `teamLanding`

### players

- `prospectsByTeam({ teamAbbr })`
- `playersByTeam({ teamAbbr, season })`

### misc

- `glossary()`, `config()`, `countries()`, `seasonSpecificRulesAndInfo()`,
  `draftYearAndRounds()`

### helpers

These make one or more requests per team and sleep `apiSleepRate` seconds
between teams to avoid rate limiting.

- `gameIdsBySeason({ season, [gameTypes], [apiSleepRate] })`
- `allPlayers({ season, [apiSleepRate] })`
- `allPlayersSummaryStatistics({ season, [apiSleepRate] })`

## Query builder

```ts
import {
  NHLClient,
  QueryBuilder,
  SeasonQuery,
  GameTypeQuery,
  PositionQuery,
  PositionTypes,
  DraftQuery,
} from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient();

const context = new QueryBuilder().build([
  new GameTypeQuery('2'),
  new SeasonQuery('20232024', '20232024'),
  new PositionQuery(PositionTypes.ALL_FORWARDS),
  new DraftQuery('2015', '1'),
]);

if (!context.isValid()) console.error(context.errors);

const { data, total } = await client.stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext({
  queryContext: context,
  reportType: 'summary',
  aggregate: true,
});
```

Available filters: `DecisionQuery`, `DraftQuery`, `ExperienceQuery`,
`FranchiseQuery`, `GameTypeQuery`, `HomeRoadQuery`, `NationalityQuery`,
`OpponentQuery`, `PositionQuery`, `SeasonQuery`, `ShootCatchesQuery`,
`StatusQuery`.

Skater report types: `summary`, `bios`, `faceoffpercentages`, `faceoffwins`,
`goalsForAgainst`, `realtime`, `penalties`, `penaltykill`, `penaltyShots`,
`powerplay`, `puckPossessions`, `summaryshooting`, `percentages`,
`scoringRates`, `scoringpergame`, `shootout`, `shottype`, `timeonice`.

## Errors

HTTP failures throw exceptions that all extend `NHLApiException`, which has
`statusCode` and `errorCode`:

| Status | Exception                    |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| 400    | `BadRequestException`        |
| 401    | `UnauthorizedException`      |
| 404    | `ResourceNotFoundException`  |
| 429    | `RateLimitExceededException` |
| 5xx    | `ServerErrorException`       |
| other  | `NHLApiException`            |

Invalid input (bad dates, unknown seasons) throws a `RangeError`.

```ts
import { ResourceNotFoundException } from 'nhl-api-ts';

try {
  await client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId: 1 });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ResourceNotFoundException) console.log(err.statusCode); // 404
}
```

## CLI

```
nhl-api-ts <module> <command> [args] [options]
```

Modules and commands are the kebab-case names of the SDK modules and methods,
and options are the kebab-case parameter names. Required parameters can be
passed positionally, in order, or as flags. Results are printed to stdout as
JSON.

```bash
nhl-api-ts --help                      # list modules
nhl-api-ts edge --help                 # list a module's commands
nhl-api-ts stats team-summary --help   # a command's arguments and options

nhl-api-ts teams teams
nhl-api-ts schedule daily-schedule --date 2024-10-09
nhl-api-ts game-center boxscore 2023020280
nhl-api-ts game-center shift-chart-data 2023020280 --excludes eventDetails,playerStats
nhl-api-ts standings league-standings --season 20222023
nhl-api-ts edge skater-detail 8478402 --season 20232024 --game-type 3
nhl-api-ts stats team-summary 20202021 20232024 --game-type-id 3 --limit 5
nhl-api-ts stats goalie-stats-summary 20232024 --stats-type advanced
nhl-api-ts helpers game-ids-by-season 20232024 --game-types 2,3
```

The query builder is available through filter flags on
`stats skater-stats-with-query-context`:

```bash
nhl-api-ts stats skater-stats-with-query-context summary \
  --season-start 20232024 --position F --nationality SWE --rookie --limit 10
```

Filter flags: `--season-start`, `--season-end`, `--franchise-id`,
`--game-type`, `--position` (F/C/L/R/D), `--nationality`, `--decision`
(W/L/O), `--draft-year`, `--draft-round`, `--rookie` / `--no-rookie`,
`--home-road` (H/R), `--opponent-franchise-id`, `--shoot-catch` (L/R),
`--active`, `--hall-of-fame`.

Global options:

| Option                  | Description                       |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `--compact`             | Print JSON on a single line       |
| `--debug`               | Log request URLs to stderr        |
| `--timeout <seconds>`   | Request timeout (default 10)      |
| `--no-follow-redirects` | Do not follow HTTP redirects      |
| `-v`, `--version`       | Print the version                 |

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` API or network error, `2` invalid usage.
Progress and warning messages from `helpers` go to stderr, so stdout is always
clean JSON.

Pipe output to `jq` to slice it:

```bash
nhl-api-ts teams teams --compact | jq -r '.[].abbr'
```

## Development

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm test         # node:test, runs the TypeScript sources directly
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint:check
pnpm build        # emits dist/
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full set of checks, and
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for repository conventions.

Try the CLI from source:

```bash
node --conditions=source src/cli.mts --help
```

<!-- Concepts: docs/concepts.md -->

# Concepts

This page covers how `nhl-api-ts` is put together and how the NHL API behaves
underneath it. Read it once before you write anything non-trivial.

## One client, nine modules

```ts
import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient({ timeout: 30 });
```

`NHLClient` holds the resolved config and one HTTP client. It exposes nine
modules. Each module is a group of endpoint methods:

| Module              | What it covers                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `client.teams`      | Team list (with conference, division, franchise id), rosters, franchises |
| `client.standings`  | League standings by date or season, season manifest                |
| `client.schedule`   | Daily, weekly, team, calendar and playoff schedules                |
| `client.gameCenter` | Boxscore, play-by-play, landing, scores, shift charts, game story  |
| `client.stats`      | Player career and game logs, team, skater and goalie stat reports  |
| `client.edge`       | NHL EDGE puck and player tracking (speed, distance, zone time, ...) |
| `client.players`    | Prospects and rosters by team                                      |
| `client.misc`       | Glossary, stats config, countries, seasons, draft rounds           |
| `client.helpers`    | Multi-request conveniences: every game id, every player, bulk stats |

The client has no state between calls: there are no caches, sessions or
cookies. Create one and reuse it, or create one per request. Both are cheap.

## Calling convention

Every endpoint method:

- is `async`,
- takes **a single options object** (or nothing), with camelCase keys,
- returns the parsed JSON body.

```ts
await client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId: 2023020280 });
await client.schedule.dailySchedule(); // all params optional
```

Responses pass through as the API returned them, with no renaming. They are
typed `JsonObject` (`Record<string, any>`) because the NHL does not publish a
schema. Only two shapes are built by the SDK:

- `Team` from `teams.teams()`: `{ conference, division, name, common_name, abbr, logo, franchise_id? }`
- `DailySchedule` from `schedule.dailySchedule()`: `{ date, nextStartDate, previousStartDate, oddsPartners, games?, numberOfGames? }`

Some methods unwrap an envelope for you: `franchises()` returns `data`,
`teamMonthlySchedule()` returns `games`, `playerGameLog()` returns `gameLog`.
The JSDoc on each method says what you get back.

## Identifier formats

| Thing        | Format        | Example      | Notes                                                    |
| ------------ | ------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Season       | `YYYYYYYY`    | `20232024`   | Start and end year, concatenated                         |
| Game id      | `YYYYTTNNNN`  | `2023020280` | Season start year, game type (`01`/`02`/`03`), game number |
| Game type    | integer       | `2`          | `1` preseason, `2` regular season, `3` playoffs          |
| Date         | `YYYY-MM-DD`  | `2024-10-09` | `dailySchedule` also accepts `2024-10-9`                 |
| Month        | `YYYY-MM`     | `2023-11`    | `teamMonthlySchedule`                                    |
| Team abbr    | 3 letters     | `TOR`        | Used by web API endpoints                                |
| Team id      | integer       | `10`         | Used by EDGE team endpoints                              |
| Franchise id | integer       | `5`          | Used by stats API filters. **Not** the same as team id   |
| Player id    | integer       | `8478402`    |                                                          |

IDs and seasons are typed `Id = string | number`, so `20232024` and
`'20232024'` both work.

Many name fields in responses are localized objects:
`{ "default": "Auston", "fr": "..." }`. Read `.default`.

## Two APIs, three base URLs

The SDK talks to two NHL services. `Endpoint` in `http-client.mts` names them:

| `Endpoint`   | Base URL                            | Used by                                     |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `API_WEB_V1` | `https://api-web.nhle.com/v1/`      | teams, standings, schedule, game center, EDGE, players, player stats |
| `API_STATS`  | `https://api.nhle.com/stats/rest/`  | franchises, shift charts, team/skater/goalie reports |
| `API_CORE`   | `https://api.nhle.com/`             | misc (glossary, config, countries, ...)     |

The **web API** is resource-shaped (`/gamecenter/{id}/boxscore`).
The **stats API** is report-shaped (`/en/skater/summary?cayenneExp=...`). It
supports filtering, sorting and pagination. See below.

[`openapi.yaml`](../openapi.yaml) describes every HTTP path the SDK calls.

## "now" and redirects

Many web API endpoints accept the literal segment `now` in place of a date or
season. The API answers with a `307` redirect to the dated resource:

```
GET /v1/standings/now                       -> 307 /v1/standings/2026-10-14
GET /v1/edge/skater-detail/8478402/now      -> 307 /v1/edge/skater-detail/8478402/20262027/2
```

When you omit `date`, `season` or `month`, the SDK sends `now`. The client
follows redirects by default (`followRedirects: true`). If you turn that off,
every `now` call fails with `NHLApiException` (status 307). See
[errors.md](errors.md#nhlapiexception-3xx).

`schedule.dailySchedule()` is the exception. It computes today's date in
**local time** and requests that date directly.

## Authentication

None. Both APIs are public and unauthenticated. The SDK sends no API keys and
reads no environment variables. `UnauthorizedException` (401) exists only so
that every status code maps to an error class.

## Configuration

```ts
new NHLClient({
  debug: false,         // log "GET: <url>" to stderr for each request
  timeout: 10,          // seconds, per request (AbortSignal.timeout)
  followRedirects: true // follow the 307s from "now" endpoints
});
```

The CLI exposes these options as `--debug`, `--timeout <seconds>` and
`--no-follow-redirects`.

## Pagination (stats API only)

The stats report endpoints take `start` (offset, default `0`) and `limit` (page
size: default `25`, or `50` for `teamSummary`). They are passed straight
through as query parameters. The API caps a page at **100 rows**, whatever
`limit` you send. `limit: -1` returns every row.

- `skaterStatsWithQueryContext` returns the full envelope `{ data, total }`, so
  you can page until you have `total` rows.
- `teamSummary`, `skaterStatsSummary` and `goalieStatsSummary` return only
  `data` (an array). Use `limit <= 100` and page until a page comes back
  shorter than `limit`.

The web API is not paginated. See
[recipes/paginate-stats.md](recipes/paginate-stats.md).

## Filtering and sorting (stats API)

The stats API filters with a `cayenneExp` expression
(`seasonId>=20232024 and positionCode='C'`) and sorts with a JSON `sort` array.

- The `*Summary` methods build `cayenneExp` from `startSeason`, `endSeason`,
  `gameTypeId` and `franchiseId`. You can replace it entirely with
  `defaultCayenneExp`.
- `skaterStatsWithQueryContext` takes a `QueryContext` built from typed filters
  by `QueryBuilder`. See
  [recipes/filter-skater-stats.md](recipes/filter-skater-stats.md).
- `sortExpr` is `SortExpr[]` (`{ property, direction }`). Each report type has
  a default sort, from `SortingOptions.getDefaultSortingForReport` and
  `goalieStatsSorts`.

## Retries and rate limits

The SDK does **not** retry. A failed request throws once. The NHL does not
document rate limits, but bursts of requests can get a `429`
(`RateLimitExceededException`) or a `5xx`. If you need retries, wrap calls
yourself. See [recipes/retries.md](recipes/retries.md).

`client.helpers` methods make one or more requests per team (30+ teams). They
sleep `apiSleepRate` seconds between teams (default 0.5 to 1 s), so a single
call can take 30 to 60 seconds. They log progress to stderr.

## Errors

HTTP errors become typed exceptions. Bad input becomes `RangeError`. Timeouts
and network failures propagate from `fetch`. The full list is in
[errors.md](errors.md).

## CLI

Every SDK method is also a CLI command:
`nhl-api-ts <module> <command> [args] [options]`. Module and command names are
the kebab-case SDK names (`gameCenter.playByPlay` becomes
`game-center play-by-play`). Output is JSON on stdout. Exit codes: `0` ok,
`1` API or network error, `2` usage error. See
[recipes/cli-and-jq.md](recipes/cli-and-jq.md).

<!-- ====================================================================== -->
<!-- Errors: docs/errors.md -->

# Errors

Everything `nhl-api-ts` can throw, why it happens, and what to do about it.

| Thrown                         | `errorCode`           | When                                       |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `BadRequestException`          | `BAD_REQUEST`         | HTTP 400 (bad `cayenneExp` or `sortExpr`)   |
| `UnauthorizedException`        | `UNAUTHORIZED`        | HTTP 401                                   |
| `ResourceNotFoundException`    | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`  | HTTP 404                                   |
| `RateLimitExceededException`   | `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | HTTP 429                                   |
| `ServerErrorException`         | `SERVER_ERROR`        | HTTP 500-599                               |
| `NHLApiException`              | `undefined`           | Any other non-2xx status, including 3xx    |
| `RangeError`                   | n/a                   | Invalid date or unknown season (client-side) |
| `DOMException` `TimeoutError`  | n/a                   | Request exceeded `timeout`                 |
| `TypeError` (`fetch failed`)   | n/a                   | DNS, TLS or connection failure             |
| `SyntaxError`                  | n/a                   | 2xx response body is not JSON              |

## The `NHLApiException` hierarchy

```ts
class NHLApiException extends Error {
  readonly statusCode: number;           // HTTP status
  readonly errorCode?: NHLApiErrorCode;  // see table above
  name: string;                          // subclass name, e.g. "ResourceNotFoundException"
}
```

All HTTP errors extend `NHLApiException`. Catch the base class to handle every
API failure, or a subclass to handle one case:

```ts
import {
  NHLApiException,
  NHLClient,
  RateLimitExceededException,
  ResourceNotFoundException,
} from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient();

try {
  await client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId: 2023020280 });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ResourceNotFoundException) {
    // bad id, or the game has no data yet
  } else if (err instanceof RateLimitExceededException) {
    // back off and retry
  } else if (err instanceof NHLApiException) {
    console.error(err.statusCode, err.errorCode, err.message);
  } else {
    throw err; // timeout, network, bug
  }
}
```

You can also switch on the code: `err.errorCode === NHLApiErrorCode.RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

**Message format:** `Request to <resource> failed`, plus `: <detail>` when the
error body is JSON with a `message` field. `<resource>` is the path relative
to the base URL (for example `gamecenter/1/boxscore`), not the full URL.
Turn on `debug: true` to log full URLs.

### `BadRequestException` (400)

**Cause:** the stats API rejected a query parameter, usually a malformed
`cayenneExp` (from `defaultCayenneExp` or a custom filter) or an unknown
property in `sortExpr`. The API's parser message is appended to the
exception message, e.g.
`Request to en/skater/summary failed: Encountered unexpected token: "=" ...`.

**Fix:** read the appended message, then fix the expression or the sort
property. Property names match the field names in the report's `data` rows.

### `UnauthorizedException` (401)

**Cause:** not expected. The NHL API is public. It can show up if a proxy or
firewall between you and the API requires auth.

**Fix:** check your network path. The SDK has no credentials to configure.

### `ResourceNotFoundException` (404)

**Cause:** the resource does not exist. Typical reasons:

- a wrong game id (it must be `YYYYTTNNNN`, e.g. `2023020280`),
- a wrong player id,
- a team id passed where an abbreviation is expected, or the reverse
  (EDGE team endpoints take `teamId`, everything else takes `teamAbbr`),
- a season or game type with no data, such as playoff data (`gameType: 3`)
  for a team that missed the playoffs.

**Fix:** check the id format in [concepts.md](concepts.md#identifier-formats).
Look up valid ids with `teams.teams()`, `teams.teamRoster()` or
`schedule.teamSeasonSchedule()`.

### `RateLimitExceededException` (429)

**Cause:** too many requests in a short window. This happens most often with
`client.helpers` or with your own loops over teams or players.

**Fix:** slow down. Raise `apiSleepRate` on helpers
(`allPlayersSummaryStatistics({ season, apiSleepRate: 2 })`). In your own
loops, add a delay and retry with backoff. See
[recipes/retries.md](recipes/retries.md). The SDK never retries on its own.

### `ServerErrorException` (5xx)

**Cause:** the NHL service failed. Two common reasons:

- An unknown report type in `skaterStatsWithQueryContext({ reportType })` or
  `goalieStatsSummary({ statsType })`. The stats API answers `500`, not `404`,
  for `/en/skater/<unknown>`. This is not transient.
- A transient outage.

**Fix:** check the report type against `SKATER_REPORT_TYPES` or the goalie
types listed on `GoalieStatsSummaryParams.statsType`. If the type is valid,
retry with backoff.

### `NHLApiException` (3xx)

**Cause:** you created the client with `followRedirects: false` and called an
endpoint that uses `now` (any call that omits `date` or `season`). The API
answers `307`, which the client does not follow, so it throws
`NHLApiException` with `statusCode: 307` and the message
`Unexpected error: Request to standings/now failed`.

**Fix:** leave `followRedirects` on (the default), or pass an explicit
`date`/`season`.

### `NHLApiException` (other statuses)

**Cause:** any status not covered above (403, 410, ...). The message starts
with `Unexpected error:`.

**Fix:** check `statusCode`. A 403 often comes from a proxy or network block, not from the NHL API itself.

## `RangeError` (invalid input)

Thrown before any request, or after a lookup request, when the input can't be
valid.

| Message                                         | Thrown by                     | Fix                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `Invalid date format. Please use YYYY-MM-DD.`   | `schedule.dailySchedule`, `normalizeDate` | Pass a real calendar date, e.g. `2024-10-09`. `2024-02-30` is rejected. |
| `Invalid Season Id <season>`                    | `standings.leagueStandings({ season })` | The season is not in `standings.seasonStandingManifest()`. Use `YYYYYYYY`, e.g. `20222023`. |

Other date parameters (`weeklySchedule`, `dailyScores`, `calendarSchedule`, ...)
are **not** validated. A bad value reaches the API and usually comes back as a
404.

## Timeouts: `DOMException` named `TimeoutError`

**Cause:** the request took longer than `timeout` seconds (default 10). The
SDK uses `AbortSignal.timeout`.

```ts
catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'TimeoutError') { ... }
}
```

**Fix:** raise the timeout (`new NHLClient({ timeout: 30 })`). Large stats
reports and play-by-play payloads can be slow.

## Network failures: `TypeError: fetch failed`

**Cause:** DNS failure, refused connection, TLS error or offline. The
underlying error is in `err.cause`.

**Fix:** check connectivity. These errors are safe to retry.

## Query builder validation

`QueryBuilder.build()` does **not** throw for invalid filters. It skips them
and collects their messages in `context.errors`:

```ts
const context = new QueryBuilder().build([new DecisionQuery('X')]);
context.isValid(); // false
context.errors;    // ['Decision value must be one of [W, L, O]']
```

Always check `context.isValid()` before you call
`skaterStatsWithQueryContext`. A skipped filter silently widens the query.

`InvalidQueryValueException` is the error that filters throw internally
during validation. The builder catches it, so it never reaches your code from
`build()`. It is exported so that custom `QueryBase` subclasses can throw it
from `validate()`.

## CLI exit codes

| Exit | Meaning                                                        | stderr starts with |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `0`  | Success. JSON on stdout                                        |                    |
| `1`  | API error (`error: <message> (HTTP <status>)`), timeout or network failure | `error:`           |
| `2`  | Usage error: unknown module or command, missing or invalid argument, invalid date, invalid filters | `error:` then help text |

<!-- ====================================================================== -->
<!-- Agent skill: skills/nhl-api-ts/SKILL.md -->

---
name: nhl-api-ts
description: Fetch NHL data (teams, rosters, schedules, scores, boxscores, play-by-play, standings, player and team stats, NHL EDGE tracking) with the nhl-api-ts TypeScript SDK or its CLI. Use when writing code or shell commands that need NHL hockey data, or when working with code that imports nhl-api-ts.
---

# Using nhl-api-ts

`nhl-api-ts` wraps the public, unauthenticated NHL APIs. It runs on Node.js
>= 24, ships as ESM only, and has no API key.

```ts
import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts';
const client = new NHLClient(); // options: { debug, timeout (s), followRedirects }
```

For a one-off lookup, the CLI is often faster than writing code:

```bash
npx nhl-api-ts <module> <command> [required args] [--options] --compact | jq ...
npx nhl-api-ts <module> <command> --help
```

## Pick the right method

| You want                                   | Call                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Team list, abbreviations, franchise ids    | `teams.teams()` returns `Team[]` with `abbr`, `name`, `franchise_id` |
| A roster                                   | `teams.teamRoster({ teamAbbr, season })` returns `{ forwards, defensemen, goalies }` |
| Games on a date                            | `schedule.dailySchedule({ date? })` returns `{ date, games?, numberOfGames? }` |
| Live or final scores for a date            | `gameCenter.dailyScores({ date? })` returns `{ games: [{ gameState, awayTeam.score, ... }] }` |
| A team's season schedule or game ids       | `schedule.teamSeasonSchedule({ teamAbbr, season })` returns `.games` |
| One game                                   | `gameCenter.boxscore` / `playByPlay` / `matchUp({ gameId })`         |
| Standings                                  | `standings.leagueStandings({ date?, season? })` returns `.standings` |
| A player's career totals or bio            | `stats.playerCareerStats({ playerId })`                              |
| A player's game-by-game log                | `stats.playerGameLog({ playerId, seasonId, gameType })`              |
| Leaderboards, filtered skater stats        | `stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext` + `QueryBuilder` (see below)     |
| Simple skater, goalie or team leaderboards | `stats.skaterStatsSummary` / `goalieStatsSummary` / `teamSummary`    |
| Speed, distance, zone time, shot speed     | `edge.*` (`skaterDetail`, `skaterSkatingSpeedDetail`, `teamDetail`, ...) |
| Every game id or every player in a season  | `helpers.gameIdsBySeason` / `helpers.allPlayers` (slow, 30+ requests) |
| Country codes for nationality filters      | `misc.countries()`                                                   |

Every method is `async` and takes **one options object** with camelCase keys.
Responses are raw NHL JSON (`JsonObject`). Name fields are localized:
read `player.firstName.default`, not `player.firstName`.

## Identifier formats (the most common source of 404s)

- Season: `20232024` (8 digits). **Not** `2023` or `2023-24`.
- Game id: `2023020280`, which is season start year + game type `02` + number.
- Game type: `1` preseason, `2` regular season, `3` playoffs.
- Date: `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `teamAbbr` (`TOR`) is used by web endpoints. `teamId` (`10`) is used by
  `edge.team*`. `franchiseId` (`5`) is used by stats filters. All three are
  different numbering schemes. Get franchise ids from `teams.teams()` (`franchise_id`).
- Omitting `date` or `season` means "current". The SDK sends `now` and follows
  the API's 307 redirect.

## Filtered stats

```ts
import { NHLClient, QueryBuilder, SeasonQuery, PositionQuery, PositionTypes, FranchiseQuery } from 'nhl-api-ts';

const queryContext = new QueryBuilder().build([
  new SeasonQuery(20232024, 20232024),
  new PositionQuery(PositionTypes.DEFENSE),
  new FranchiseQuery(5),
]);
if (!queryContext.isValid()) throw new Error(queryContext.errors.join('; '));

const { data, total } = await client.stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext({
  queryContext, reportType: 'summary', limit: 100,
});
```

Other filters: `GameTypeQuery`, `NationalityQuery('SWE')`, `DraftQuery(year, round?)`,
`ExperienceQuery(isRookie)`, `HomeRoadQuery('H'|'R')`, `OpponentQuery(franchiseId)`,
`ShootCatchesQuery('L'|'R')`, `DecisionQuery('W'|'L'|'O')`, `StatusQuery({ isActive, isHallOfFame })`.
Report types: `SKATER_REPORT_TYPES` (`summary`, `realtime`, `timeonice`, `powerplay`, ...).
An unknown report type makes the API return 500.

## Gotchas

- **The stats API pages are capped at 100 rows.** A larger `limit` is cut to
  100. Page with `start: rows.length` until you have `total` rows, or pass
  `limit: -1` to get everything (undocumented).
- `stats.*Summary` methods return just the `data` array. `skaterStatsWithQueryContext`
  returns `{ data, total }`.
- `helpers.gameIdsBySeason` returns each game twice (once per team), so dedupe
  with `new Set`. Helpers sleep between teams and take 30 to 60 seconds.
- `dailySchedule()` with no date uses **local** time. Pass a date on UTC servers.
- `games` and `numberOfGames` are **missing** on days with no games, so use `?? []`.
- No built-in retries. On `RateLimitExceededException` (429) or
  `ServerErrorException` (5xx), back off and retry. Don't `Promise.all` over
  all 32 teams.
- `QueryBuilder.build` drops invalid filters silently. Always check `isValid()`.

## Errors

All HTTP errors extend `NHLApiException` (`statusCode`, `errorCode`):
`ResourceNotFoundException` 404, `RateLimitExceededException` 429,
`ServerErrorException` 5xx, `BadRequestException` 400 (bad `cayenneExp` or
`sort`). Bad dates or unknown seasons throw `RangeError`. Timeouts throw
`DOMException` with `name === 'TimeoutError'`.

## Testing code that uses it

Mock `globalThis.fetch`. The SDK looks it up on every request:
`mock.method(globalThis, 'fetch', async () => Response.json({...}))`.

## More

- Concepts: `docs/concepts.md`. Errors: `docs/errors.md`. Recipes: `docs/recipes/`
- Full public API surface: `api-report.md`. HTTP paths: `openapi.yaml`
- Everything in one file: `llms-full.txt`

<!-- Filter skater stats: docs/recipes/filter-skater-stats.md -->

# Filter skater stats with the query builder

Use `QueryBuilder` with `skaterStatsWithQueryContext` for questions like
"Swedish rookie forwards in 2023-24, by points". You don't have to write
`cayenneExp` strings by hand.

```ts
import {
  ExperienceQuery,
  GameTypeQuery,
  NationalityQuery,
  NHLClient,
  PositionQuery,
  PositionTypes,
  QueryBuilder,
  SeasonQuery,
} from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient();

const queryContext = new QueryBuilder().build([
  new SeasonQuery(20232024, 20232024),
  new GameTypeQuery(2),
  new PositionQuery(PositionTypes.ALL_FORWARDS),
  new NationalityQuery('SWE'),
  new ExperienceQuery(true),
]);

if (!queryContext.isValid()) {
  throw new Error(queryContext.errors.join('; '));
}

const { data, total } = await client.stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext({
  queryContext,
  reportType: 'summary',
  limit: 10,
});
```

`queryContext.queryStr` is the generated `cayenneExp`:

```
seasonId >= 20232024 and seasonId <= 20232024 and gameTypeId=2 and (positionCode='L' or positionCode='R' or positionCode='C') and nationalityCode='SWE' and isRookie='1'
```

## Filters

| Filter                                    | Produces                                  | Values                                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `new SeasonQuery(start, end)`             | `seasonId >= start and seasonId <= end`   | `YYYYYYYY`                                  |
| `new GameTypeQuery(type)`                 | `gameTypeId=type`                         | `1`, `2`, `3`                               |
| `new PositionQuery(position)`             | `positionCode='C'` (or an OR group for `F`) | `PositionTypes.CENTER`, `LEFT_WING`, `RIGHT_WING`, `DEFENSE`, `ALL_FORWARDS` |
| `new FranchiseQuery(id)`                  | `franchiseId=id`                          | franchise id (from `teams.franchises()`)    |
| `new OpponentQuery(id)`                   | `opponentFranchiseId=id`                  | franchise id                                |
| `new NationalityQuery(code)`              | `nationalityCode='SWE'`                   | 3-letter code (from `misc.countries()`)     |
| `new DraftQuery(year, round?)`            | `draftYear=2015 and draftRound=1`         |                                             |
| `new ExperienceQuery(isRookie)`           | `isRookie='1'` / `'0'`                    | boolean                                     |
| `new HomeRoadQuery(hr)`                   | `homeRoad='H'`                            | `H`, `R`                                    |
| `new ShootCatchesQuery(lr)`               | `shootsCatches='L'`                       | `L`, `R`                                    |
| `new DecisionQuery(d)`                    | `decision='W'`                            | `W`, `L`, `O` (validated)                   |
| `new StatusQuery({ isActive, isHallOfFame })` | `active=1` / `isInHallOfFame=1`       | Hall of Fame wins if both are set           |

Filters are joined with `and`. Invalid filters (only `DecisionQuery` validates
today) are left out and reported in `queryContext.errors`. **Check
`isValid()`**, or the query silently matches more rows than you meant.

## Report types

`reportType` picks the report: `summary`, `bios`, `faceoffpercentages`,
`faceoffwins`, `goalsForAgainst`, `realtime`, `penalties`, `penaltykill`,
`penaltyShots`, `powerplay`, `puckPossessions`, `summaryshooting`,
`percentages`, `scoringRates`, `scoringpergame`, `shootout`, `shottype`,
`timeonice`. The list is exported as `SKATER_REPORT_TYPES`. Each report has a
default sort. Pass `sortExpr` to override it:

```ts
await client.stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext({
  queryContext,
  reportType: 'realtime',
  sortExpr: [
    { property: 'hits', direction: 'DESC' },
    { property: 'playerId', direction: 'ASC' },
  ],
});
```

An unknown `reportType` makes the API answer `500` (`ServerErrorException`).

## Aggregate across seasons

With a multi-season `SeasonQuery`, you get one row per player per season. Pass
`aggregate: true` to get one row per player:

```ts
const career = new QueryBuilder().build([new SeasonQuery(20182019, 20232024)]);
await client.stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext({
  queryContext: career,
  reportType: 'summary',
  aggregate: true,
});
```

## From the CLI

```bash
nhl-api-ts stats skater-stats-with-query-context summary \
  --season-start 20232024 --game-type 2 --position F --nationality SWE --rookie --limit 10
```

Goalies don't have a query-builder method. Use `goalieStatsSummary` with
`franchiseId` or `defaultCayenneExp`.

Runnable version: [`examples/query-builder.mts`](../../examples/query-builder.mts).

<!-- Paginate stats: docs/recipes/paginate-stats.md -->

# Paginate stats reports

The stats API endpoints (`client.stats.teamSummary`, `skaterStatsSummary`,
`skaterStatsWithQueryContext`, `goalieStatsSummary`) are paged with `start`
(offset) and `limit` (page size). The web API endpoints are not paged.

> **The stats API returns at most 100 rows per request.** A larger `limit`
> is silently capped at 100. `limit: -1` returns every row in one request.

## With a total: `skaterStatsWithQueryContext`

This method returns the whole envelope, `{ data, total }`. Advance by the
number of rows you actually received, not by `limit`:

```ts
import { NHLClient, QueryBuilder, SeasonQuery } from 'nhl-api-ts';
import type { JsonObject } from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient();
const queryContext = new QueryBuilder().build([
  new SeasonQuery(20232024, 20232024),
]);

const rows: JsonObject[] = [];
while (true) {
  const page = await client.stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext({
    queryContext,
    reportType: 'summary',
    start: rows.length,
    limit: 100,
  });
  rows.push(...page.data);
  if (page.data.length === 0 || rows.length >= page.total) {
    break;
  }
}
console.log(`${rows.length} skaters`);
```

## Without a total: the `*Summary` methods

`teamSummary`, `skaterStatsSummary` and `goalieStatsSummary` return only the
`data` array. Use `limit` of 100 or less, and stop when a page comes back
shorter than `limit`:

```ts
const limit = 100;
const goalies: JsonObject[] = [];
while (true) {
  const page = await client.stats.goalieStatsSummary({
    startSeason: 20232024,
    start: goalies.length,
    limit,
  });
  goalies.push(...page);
  if (page.length < limit) {
    break;
  }
}
```

With a `limit` above 100, the first page is capped at 100 rows, so
`page.length < limit` holds right away and the loop stops after one page.

## Everything at once

```ts
const all = await client.stats.skaterStatsSummary({
  startSeason: 20232024,
  endSeason: 20232024,
  limit: -1,
});
```

This is one request. It works today but isn't documented by the NHL. Page
explicitly if you need it to keep working.

## Notes

- Keep the sort stable across pages. Every default sort ends on a unique key
  (`playerId` or `teamId`), so rows don't shift between pages. If you pass
  your own `sortExpr`, end it with `{ property: 'playerId', direction: 'ASC' }`.
- From the CLI: `--start` and `--limit` on any `stats` command.

Runnable version: [`examples/paginate-stats.mts`](../../examples/paginate-stats.mts).

<!-- Today's games and live scores: docs/recipes/live-scores.md -->

# Today's games and live scores

## Today's schedule

```ts
import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient();

const today = await client.schedule.dailySchedule();
console.log(today.date, today.numberOfGames ?? 0);
for (const game of today.games ?? []) {
  console.log(game.id, game.awayTeam.abbrev, '@', game.homeTeam.abbrev, game.gameState);
}
```

`dailySchedule()` with no date uses **local** today. On a server running in
UTC, "today" can roll over before North American games finish. Pass an
explicit date when that matters: `dailySchedule({ date: '2024-10-09' })`.
`games` and `numberOfGames` are missing (not empty) on days with no games.

## Scores for a day

```ts
const scores = await client.gameCenter.dailyScores(); // "now" -> redirect to today
for (const game of scores.games ?? []) {
  console.log(
    `${game.awayTeam.abbrev} ${game.awayTeam.score ?? '-'} @ ${game.homeTeam.abbrev} ${game.homeTeam.score ?? '-'}  ${game.gameState}`,
  );
}
```

`gameState` values you'll see: `FUT` (scheduled), `PRE` (pregame), `LIVE`,
`CRIT` (final minutes of a close game), `FINAL`, `OFF` (official/final).

## One game in detail

```ts
const gameId = 2023020280;
const landing = await client.gameCenter.matchUp({ gameId });   // summary, scoring by period, three stars
const box = await client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId });      // per-player stats
const pbp = await client.gameCenter.playByPlay({ gameId });    // every event
```

## Polling

There is no push or websocket API. Poll `dailyScores()` or
`matchUp({ gameId })`, and keep the interval reasonable (15 to 30 seconds) so
you don't hit rate limits.

```ts
import { setTimeout as delay } from 'node:timers/promises';

while (true) {
  const { games = [] } = await client.gameCenter.dailyScores();
  if (games.every((game: { gameState: string }) => ['FINAL', 'OFF'].includes(game.gameState))) {
    break;
  }
  // render...
  await delay(30_000);
}
```

## CLI

```bash
nhl-api-ts schedule daily-schedule --compact | jq '.games[] | {id, away: .awayTeam.abbrev, home: .homeTeam.abbrev}'
nhl-api-ts game-center daily-scores --date 2024-10-09 --compact | jq '.games[] | [.awayTeam.abbrev, .awayTeam.score, .homeTeam.abbrev, .homeTeam.score]'
```

Runnable version: [`examples/todays-games.mts`](../../examples/todays-games.mts).

<!-- Season-wide data: docs/recipes/season-wide-data.md -->

# Collect season-wide data (every game, every player)

`client.helpers` puts together data that the API only serves one team at a
time. Each method makes 30+ requests and sleeps between teams, so expect one
call to take 30 to 60 seconds. Progress messages go to stderr.

## Every game id in a season

```ts
import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts';

const client = new NHLClient();

const ids = await client.helpers.gameIdsBySeason({
  season: 20232024,
  gameTypes: [2], // regular season only. Omit for all game types
});
const unique = [...new Set(ids)]; // each game appears once per team
```

`gameIdsBySeason` reads every team's season schedule, so each game shows up
twice (home and away). Always dedupe.

## Every rostered player

```ts
const players = await client.helpers.allPlayers({ season: 20232024 });
// each player: roster fields + team: 'TOR', firstName: 'Auston', lastName: 'Matthews'
```

`firstName` and `lastName` are flattened from `{ default: '...' }` to plain
strings. `team` is the abbreviation of the roster the player was listed on.
A player on more than one roster in the season appears once per roster.

## Skater stats merged with roster info

```ts
const rows = await client.helpers.allPlayersSummaryStatistics({
  season: 20232024,
  apiSleepRate: 1.5, // slower = fewer 429s
});
```

This method calls `allPlayers`, then the skater summary report per franchise,
then merges the two by player id. Stat fields win when keys collide. Goalies
are not included, because the skater summary report has none.

## Without helpers: one team at a time

When you only need some teams, call the endpoints directly. You make fewer
requests:

```ts
const schedule = await client.schedule.teamSeasonSchedule({
  teamAbbr: 'TOR',
  season: 20232024,
});
const gameIds = schedule.games
  .filter((game: { gameType: number }) => game.gameType === 2)
  .map((game: { id: number }) => game.id);
```

## Tuning

- `apiSleepRate` is the number of seconds to sleep before each team's request.
  Defaults: `gameIdsBySeason` 1, `allPlayers` 0.5,
  `allPlayersSummaryStatistics` 1. Raise it if you get
  `RateLimitExceededException`.
- Cache the results. Past seasons don't change.
- From the CLI: `nhl-api-ts helpers game-ids-by-season 20232024 --game-types 2 --api-sleep-rate 1.5`.

<!-- ====================================================================== -->
<!-- Retries: docs/recipes/retries.md -->

# Retry on rate limits and server errors

The SDK makes exactly one attempt per call. Wrap calls yourself when you loop
over many teams, players or games.

```ts
import {
  NHLApiException,
  NHLClient,
  RateLimitExceededException,
  ServerErrorException,
} from 'nhl-api-ts';
import { setTimeout as delay } from 'node:timers/promises';

const isRetryable = (err: unknown): boolean =>
  err instanceof RateLimitExceededException ||
  err instanceof ServerErrorException ||
  (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'TimeoutError') ||
  (err instanceof TypeError && err.message === 'fetch failed');

export async function withRetry<T>(
  call: () => Promise<T>,
  { attempts = 4, baseMs = 500 } = {},
): Promise<T> {
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await call();
    } catch (err) {
      if (attempt >= attempts || !isRetryable(err)) {
        throw err;
      }
      // exponential backoff with jitter: 500ms, 1s, 2s, ...
      await delay(baseMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1) * (0.5 + Math.random()));
    }
  }
}

const client = new NHLClient();
const boxscore = await withRetry(() =>
  client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId: 2023020280 }),
);
```

## What to retry

| Error                                   | Retry? | Why                                            |
| --------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `RateLimitExceededException` (429)      | yes    | Back off first                                 |
| `ServerErrorException` (5xx)            | yes, a few times | Unless `reportType` is unknown, which always 500s |
| `TimeoutError`                          | yes    | Or raise `timeout`                             |
| `TypeError: fetch failed`               | yes    | Network blip                                   |
| `ResourceNotFoundException` (404)       | no     | The id or date is wrong                        |
| `BadRequestException` (400)             | no     | The query is wrong                             |
| `RangeError`                            | no     | The input is invalid                           |

## Pace bulk loops

For loops over all teams, a fixed pause between requests prevents most 429s.
`client.helpers` methods already do this through `apiSleepRate`:

```ts
for (const team of await client.teams.teams()) {
  const roster = await withRetry(() =>
    client.teams.teamRoster({ teamAbbr: team.abbr, season: 20232024 }),
  );
  // ...
  await delay(500);
}
```

Don't fire 32 requests with `Promise.all`. Keep concurrency low (2 to 4) if you
need parallelism.

Runnable version: [`examples/error-handling.mts`](../../examples/error-handling.mts).

<!-- ====================================================================== -->
<!-- CLI and jq: docs/recipes/cli-and-jq.md -->

# Use the CLI with jq

Every SDK method is a CLI command. Output is JSON on stdout. Errors and
progress go to stderr, so you can pipe stdout safely.

```bash
npx nhl-api-ts --help
nhl-api-ts <module> <command> [required args...] [--options]
```

Name mapping: `client.gameCenter.playByPlay({ gameId })` becomes
`nhl-api-ts game-center play-by-play <game-id>`. Required params can be
positional, in the order the help lists them, or flags. Optional params are
always flags: `teamAbbr` becomes `--team-abbr`.

## Examples

```bash
# Team abbreviations
nhl-api-ts teams teams --compact | jq -r '.[].abbr'

# Map abbreviations to franchise ids (needed for stats filters)
nhl-api-ts teams teams --compact | jq -r '.[] | "\(.abbr)\t\(.franchise_id)"'

# Top 5 point scorers for one franchise (5 = Toronto) in 2023-24
nhl-api-ts stats skater-stats-summary 20232024 20232024 --franchise-id 5 --limit 5 --compact \
  | jq -r '.[] | "\(.skaterFullName)\t\(.points)"'

# Goals in a game, in order
nhl-api-ts game-center play-by-play 2023020280 --compact \
  | jq '[.plays[] | select(.typeDescKey == "goal") | {period: .periodDescriptor.number, time: .timeInPeriod}]'

# Conference standings
nhl-api-ts standings league-standings --date 2024-04-18 --compact \
  | jq -r '.standings[] | select(.conferenceAbbrev == "E") | "\(.teamAbbrev.default)\t\(.points)"'

# EDGE: max skating speed, playoffs
nhl-api-ts edge skater-skating-speed-detail 8478402 --season 20232024 --game-type 3

# Query builder via filter flags
nhl-api-ts stats skater-stats-with-query-context summary \
  --season-start 20232024 --position D --nationality FIN --limit 10
```

## Options that take structured values

| Type     | Example                                                        |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| list     | `--excludes eventDetails,playerStats`                          |
| int list | `--game-types 2,3`                                             |
| JSON     | `--sort-expr '[{"property":"goals","direction":"DESC"}]'`      |
| boolean  | `--aggregate` / `--no-aggregate`, `--rookie` / `--no-rookie`   |

## Scripting

- Check the exit code: `0` ok, `1` API or network error, `2` usage error.
- `--compact` prints one line, which is faster to pipe.
- `--debug` logs every request URL to stderr.
- `--timeout 30` for slow reports.
- `nhl-api-ts ... | head` exits cleanly. EPIPE is handled.

```bash
if ! out=$(nhl-api-ts game-center boxscore "$id" --compact 2>err.log); then
  echo "failed: $(cat err.log)"; exit 1
fi
```

<!-- ====================================================================== -->
<!-- Testing: docs/recipes/testing.md -->

# Test code that uses the SDK

The SDK calls the global `fetch`, which it looks up on every request. Your
tests can replace it, so they don't need network access or a special client.

## node:test

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { afterEach, it, mock } from 'node:test';
import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts';

afterEach(() => mock.restoreAll());

it('lists team abbreviations', async () => {
  const fetchMock = mock.method(globalThis, 'fetch', async (input: string | URL) => {
    const url = String(input);
    const body = url.includes('/standings/')
      ? { standings: [{ teamAbbrev: { default: 'TOR' }, teamName: { default: 'Toronto Maple Leafs' } }] }
      : { data: [{ id: 5, fullName: 'Toronto Maple Leafs' }] };
    return Response.json(body);
  });

  const teams = await new NHLClient().teams.teams();

  assert.deepEqual(teams.map((team) => team.abbr), ['TOR']);
  assert.equal(teams[0].franchise_id, 5);
  assert.equal(String(fetchMock.mock.calls[0].arguments[0]), 'https://api-web.nhle.com/v1/standings/now');
});
```

## Vitest or Jest

```ts
vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch').mockResolvedValue(Response.json({ data: [] }));
```

## Simulating errors

Return a non-2xx `Response`. The SDK maps it to the matching exception:

```ts
mock.method(globalThis, 'fetch', async () =>
  Response.json({ message: 'nope' }, { status: 429 }),
);
await assert.rejects(
  new NHLClient().misc.countries(),
  { name: 'RateLimitExceededException', statusCode: 429 },
);
```

## Tips

- Assert on URLs. They are the stable contract. Response payloads are the
  NHL's and can change without notice.
- Record real responses once with `--debug` and a CLI call
  (`nhl-api-ts game-center boxscore 2023020280 > fixtures/boxscore.json`),
  then serve them from your mock.
- `client.helpers` methods sleep between teams. Pass `apiSleepRate: 0` in tests.

<!-- Migration guide: MIGRATION.md -->

# Migration guide

Guides for moving between versions of `nhl-api-ts`, and from the Python
library it was ported from. Newest first.

- [Unreleased: functional API (planned)](#unreleased-functional-api-planned)
- [nhl-api-py → nhl-api-ts 0.1](#nhl-api-py--nhl-api-ts-01)

---

## Unreleased: functional API (planned)

Not released. A refactor from classes to plain functions is planned in
[`.claude/plans/functional-refactor.md`](.claude/plans/functional-refactor.md).
When it lands, its before/after guide goes here. The planned changes:

| 0.1                                           | Planned                                         |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `new NHLClient(options)`                      | `createNHLClient(options)`                      |
| `new QueryBuilder().build([...])`             | `buildQuery([...])`                             |
| `new SeasonQuery(a, b)`, `new PositionQuery(p)`, ... | `filter.season(a, b)`, `filter.position(p)`, ... |
| `context.isValid()`                           | `isValidQuery(context)`                         |
| `context.queryStr`                            | `context.query`                                 |
| `SortingOptions.getDefaultSortingForReport(r)`| `defaultSortForReport(r)`                       |
| `InvalidQueryValueException`                  | removed (validation errors stay in `context.errors`) |
| `HttpClient`, `ClientConfig`                  | `createGet`, `resolveConfig`                    |

`client.<module>.<method>(...)` calls are planned to stay the same.

---

## nhl-api-py → nhl-api-ts 0.1

`nhl-api-ts` calls the same endpoints as
[nhl-api-py](https://github.com/coreyjs/nhl-api-py) and returns the same
payloads. The changes are in the calling convention.

### Install and import

```diff
- pip install nhl-api-py
+ pnpm add nhl-api-ts         # Node.js >= 24, ESM only
```

```diff
- from nhlpy import NHLClient
- client = NHLClient()
+ import { NHLClient } from 'nhl-api-ts';
+ const client = new NHLClient();
```

### Calls are async, camelCase, and take one object

Module and method names go from snake_case to camelCase. Keyword arguments
become keys of a single options object. Every call returns a promise.

```diff
- client.game_center.boxscore(game_id="2023020280")
+ await client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId: '2023020280' })

- client.edge.skater_detail(player_id=8478402, season=20232024, game_type=3)
+ await client.edge.skaterDetail({ playerId: 8478402, season: 20232024, gameType: 3 })

- client.stats.team_summary(start_season="20202021", end_season="20232024", is_aggregate=True)
+ await client.stats.teamSummary({ startSeason: 20202021, endSeason: 20232024, isAggregate: true })

- client.helpers.all_players(season="20232024", api_sleep_rate=1)
+ await client.helpers.allPlayers({ season: 20232024, apiSleepRate: 1 })
```

| Python module            | TypeScript module     |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- |
| `client.game_center`     | `client.gameCenter`   |
| `client.teams`, `client.standings`, `client.schedule`, `client.stats`, `client.edge`, `client.players`, `client.misc`, `client.helpers` | same names |

Method renames follow the same rule (`play_by_play` → `playByPlay`,
`goalie_5v5_detail` → `goalie5v5Detail`). No method was added, removed or
renamed beyond the case change.

IDs and seasons accept `string | number`.

### Client options

```diff
- NHLClient(debug=True, timeout=30, follow_redirects=True, ssl_verify=False)
+ new NHLClient({ debug: true, timeout: 30, followRedirects: true })
```

`ssl_verify` was removed. Node's `fetch` has no per-request switch for TLS
verification. If you need it, set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` for the
process. That is a Node setting, not one the SDK reads, and you should only use
it for local debugging. `debug` logs go to stderr, not the Python `logging`
module.

### Query builder

Import everything from the package root. The classes and their constructor
arguments are the same.

```diff
- from nhlpy.api.query.builder import QueryBuilder
- from nhlpy.api.query.filters.season import SeasonQuery
- from nhlpy.api.query.filters.position import PositionQuery, PositionTypes
- context = QueryBuilder().build(filters=[SeasonQuery(season_start="20232024", season_end="20232024"),
-                                         PositionQuery(position=PositionTypes.CENTER)])
- if not context.is_valid(): print(context.errors)
- client.stats.skater_stats_with_query_context(query_context=context, report_type="summary")
+ import { PositionQuery, PositionTypes, QueryBuilder, SeasonQuery } from 'nhl-api-ts';
+ const context = new QueryBuilder().build([
+   new SeasonQuery(20232024, 20232024),
+   new PositionQuery(PositionTypes.CENTER),
+ ]);
+ if (!context.isValid()) console.error(context.errors);
+ await client.stats.skaterStatsWithQueryContext({ queryContext: context, reportType: 'summary' });
```

| Python                      | TypeScript                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `context.query_str`         | `context.queryStr`        |
| `context.fact_query`        | `context.factQuery`       |
| `context.is_valid()`        | `context.isValid()`       |
| `QueryBuilder(debug=True)`  | `new QueryBuilder({ debug: true })` |
| `StatusQuery(is_active=True)` | `new StatusQuery({ isActive: true })` |

Behavior fix: in nhl-api-py, `DecisionQuery.validate()` returns `None`, so the
builder rejects every decision filter, valid ones included. In nhl-api-ts,
`new DecisionQuery('W')` is accepted, and only values other than `W`, `L` and
`O` are rejected.

### Errors

The exception class names are the same. They are exported from the package
root. Python `ValueError` for bad input becomes `RangeError`.

```diff
- from nhlpy.http_client import ResourceNotFoundException
- try:
-     client.game_center.boxscore(game_id="1")
- except ResourceNotFoundException as e:
-     print(e.status_code)
+ import { ResourceNotFoundException } from 'nhl-api-ts';
+ try {
+   await client.gameCenter.boxscore({ gameId: 1 });
+ } catch (err) {
+   if (err instanceof ResourceNotFoundException) console.log(err.statusCode);
+ }
```

| Python          | TypeScript    |
| --------------- | ------------- |
| `e.status_code` | `err.statusCode` |
| `e.error_code`  | `err.errorCode`  |
| `ValueError`    | `RangeError`     |

Timeouts surface as a `DOMException` named `TimeoutError`, not
`httpx.TimeoutException`. See [docs/errors.md](docs/errors.md).

### Payloads

Response bodies are unchanged and keep the NHL's camelCase keys. The shapes
the SDK builds itself keep their Python key names: `teams.teams()` returns
`common_name` and `franchise_id`.

### Output

`helpers` progress and warning messages go to **stderr**. The CLI's stdout is
always pure JSON.

### New in the port

- A CLI: `npx nhl-api-ts <module> <command>`. See the [README](README.md#cli).
- Full TypeScript types for every parameter object.
